profile.faq.heading: Questions about these changes
profile.faq.updateEmailQ: What happens when I change my email address?
profile.faq.updateEmailA: We send a confirmation link to the new address and leave your account on the old one until you follow it. Once confirmed, the new address is what you sign in with, and every order confirmation, payment link and invoice goes there.
profile.faq.whenAppliesQ: When does the change take effect?
profile.faq.whenAppliesA: The moment the link is followed, and not before. Confirming an email address also signs you out on every device, because the address is your sign-in identity — sign back in with the new one.
profile.faq.historyQ: Do I lose my order history?
profile.faq.historyA: No. Your orders, invoices, saved addresses, scheduled orders and saved cards all stay exactly as they are. Changing a contact detail changes where we write to you and nothing else.
profile.faq.phoneCodeQ: Why does the number confirmation arrive by email?
profile.faq.phoneCodeA: This store has no text-message provider configured, so the link is sent to your email address instead. It proves the change came from you, which is what stops somebody else altering the number on your account.
profile.faq.ordersInFlightQ: What about an order that is already on its way?
profile.faq.ordersInFlightA: It is unaffected. An order keeps the delivery details captured when it was placed, so changing a number here does not redirect a delivery already in progress. Contact us if a delivery has to be redirected.

erp.system.customDescription: Anything with a documented HTTP API. REST and JSON by default, with OData and GraphQL where your system speaks them.
erp.auth.clientCredentialsNote: A machine-to-machine grant with no person involved. The right answer for SAP, and it keeps working when staff change.
erp.auth.authorizationCodeNote: You sign in to your own system and approve the permissions listed. Nothing here ever sees your password.
erp.auth.apiKeyNote: A key your system issues, sent with every request. Tell us the header or parameter name it expects.
erp.auth.bearerTokenNote: A token sent in the Authorization header. Simple, and it has to be replaced by hand when it expires.
erp.auth.basicNote: Offered because some systems still require it. It has no expiry and no scope, so use one of the others where your system allows it.
erp.auth.mondayPersonalTokenNote: Carries one person's whole monday.com account and does not stop working when they leave. Test connections only.
erp.network.publicHttpsNote: Your system answers on a public HTTPS address. Nothing for your IT team to open up.

erp.network.sapCloudConnectorNote: Your SAP is on-premise and reached through a connector you run. Give us the connector's address, not SAP's.

erp.role.integrationManagerNote: As an integration manager you can set up and run the connection. Only an owner can change who has access.

carrier.DHL.title: Your DHL account
carrier.DHL.description: Connect your own DHL business account for rates, labels, pickup booking and tracking. You can send parcels with DHL without connecting it, by booking them yourself.
carrier.DHL.accountNumberHint: The number on your DHL invoices. It is not a secret.
carrier.DHL.step1: Ask DHL Express for MyDHL API access for your business account.
carrier.DHL.step2: Enter your DHL account number, then the API key and secret that DHL gives you.
carrier.DHL.step3: Test the connection. It counts as connected only after a real test with DHL passes and you switch it on.
carrier.FEDEX.title: Your FedEx account
carrier.FEDEX.description: Connect your own FedEx business account for rates, labels, pickup booking and tracking. You can send parcels with FedEx without connecting it, by booking them yourself.
carrier.FEDEX.accountNumberHint: The nine-digit number on your FedEx invoices. It is not a secret.
carrier.FEDEX.step1: Create a project on the FedEx Developer Portal and link your FedEx account to it.
carrier.FEDEX.step2: Enter your FedEx account number, then the API key and secret key from that project.
carrier.FEDEX.step3: Test the connection. It counts as connected only after a real test with FedEx passes and you switch it on.
carrier.INDIA_POST.title: Your India Post business account
carrier.INDIA_POST.description: Send parcels with India Post by booking them at a post office or through India Post itself, then record the tracking number here.
carrier.INDIA_POST.noApiNotice: India Post has no official API to connect to, so there is nothing to connect here. Book the parcel with India Post yourself and enter its tracking number on the order. Rates, labels, pickup booking and automatic tracking are not available.
carrier.INDIA_POST.step1: Book the parcel with India Post, for example Speed Post, at a post office or through your India Post business account.
carrier.INDIA_POST.step2: Enter the article number that India Post gives you on the order, so you and the buyer can follow it on the India Post tracking page.
carrier.notConnectedNotice: API account not connected. You can still assign this carrier using manual/offline booking, but automatic rates, labels, pickup booking and carrier tracking will remain unavailable until valid credentials are connected.
